_note: Sentence-segmentation conformance cases for PRD §6.1 (task 0.8). `sentences` is the exact list `segmentSentences(text)` must return, trimmed of the whitespace around each sentence; its length is the sentence count. Plain text only: no Markdown, so the same cases run against the rule-based fallback (task 0.9) and inside each real webview (task 6.2).

cases.rule: Two ordinary sentences split at the period.
cases.text: The pen was full. The page was empty.

cases.rule: Three short sentences.
cases.text: First. Second. Third.

cases.rule: Text without terminal punctuation is one sentence.
cases.text: One sentence with no terminator

cases.rule: §6.1: `Dr.` does not split.
cases.text: Dr. Smith went home. He slept.

cases.rule: §6.1: `e.g.` does not split.
cases.text: See e.g. the chart. Next.

cases.rule: §6.1: `i.e.` does not split.
cases.text: He cited i.e. the second law. Then he stopped.
sentences: He cited i.e. the second law.

cases.rule: §6.1: `Mr.` and `Mrs.` do not split, twice in a row.
cases.text: Mr. and Mrs. Halloway arrived. They stayed.

cases.rule: §6.1: `Ms.` does not split.
cases.text: Ms. Jones signed it. The deal closed.

cases.rule: §6.1: `vs.` does not split.
cases.text: Cats vs. dogs is an old argument. Nobody wins.
sentences: Cats vs. dogs is an old argument.

cases.rule: §6.1: `etc.` does not split — so a sentence that really ends in `etc.` is joined to the next one. Stated limit, not a bug.
cases.text: Bring paper, ink, blotters, etc. Then start.
sentences: Bring paper, ink, blotters, etc. Then start.

cases.rule: An abbreviation away from any boundary changes nothing.
cases.text: The e.g. in that line is wrong.
sentences: The e.g. in that line is wrong.

cases.rule: §6.1: a single capital letter followed by a period is an initial, not a boundary.
cases.text: A. Smith wrote it. B. Jones edited it.

cases.rule: Three initials in a row are all held together.
cases.text: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote it. He was a don.
sentences: J. R. R. Tolkien wrote it.

cases.rule: §6.1: a decimal number does not split.
cases.text: It cost 3.50 dollars. Then more.

cases.rule: A decimal that ends the sentence still splits after it.
cases.text: The bill came to 3.50. Then we left.

cases.rule: A decimal below one (leading zero) does not split.
cases.text: Ink flows at 0.5 ml per hour. That is slow.
sentences: Ink flows at 0.5 ml per hour.

cases.rule: Version numbers do not split.
cases.text: Version 2.0 shipped late. Version 3.0 did not.

cases.rule: An integer followed by a period and a capital is a boundary: only digit-period-digit is a decimal.
cases.text: Chapter 4. The Pen Arrives. It was late.

cases.rule: A question mark ends a sentence.
cases.text: Where is the ink? It is on the desk.

cases.rule: An exclamation mark ends a sentence.
cases.text: Stop! The nib is dry.

cases.rule: An ellipsis inside a sentence is not a boundary.
cases.text: He waited... then he wrote. The page filled.

cases.rule: A soft line break between sentences is a boundary and is not part of either sentence.
cases.text:
Line one.
Line two.

cases.rule: Two spaces between sentences are trimmed off both.
cases.text: Two spaces follow.  The next begins.

cases.rule: A quoted clause closed before the period keeps its sentence whole.
cases.text: "The nib is dry," she said. Then she left.

cases.rule: A closing quote after the terminal period stays with the sentence it ends.
cases.text: He said "stop." Then he left.

cases.rule: A parenthetical inside a sentence is not a boundary.
cases.text: The nib (a fine one) was dry. He replaced it.
sentences: The nib (a fine one) was dry.

cases.rule: The periods inside a URL are not boundaries.
cases.text: Visit https://example.com/a.b today. Then leave.

cases.rule: Trailing whitespace is not part of the last sentence.
cases.text: Done.

cases.rule: Whitespace-only text has no sentences.
Empty text has no sentences.
